newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK ALUMINIUM/ATTICA TO ISSUE 5-YR CONVERTIBLES.
newsitem.headline: GREEK ALUMINIUM/ATTICA TO ISSUE 5-YR CONVERTIBLES.

text.p: Greek metallurgical firm Aluminium of Attica will issue a five-year convertible bond worth 2.329 billion drachmas following the approval by its general shareholders meeting on Tuesday, it said in a statement.
The firm will issue 970.667 bonds with a face value of 2,400 drachmas convertible into common registered shares, it said.
The bond will carry an annual coupon based on one-year Athibor minus 400 basis points and fixed, it said.
Each shareholder will have the right to buy a trading unit of 40 bonds for 300 common registered shares outstanding. The offer price is 2,400 drachmas per bond.
The conversion ratio is 40 convertible bonds for 40 common registered shares, it added.
The stated conversion price will be equal to 3,000 drachmas per share for the life of the bond, it said.
"The bonds that have not being converted into stocks will be called gradually from the end of the second year until maturity," it said.

For every 40 bonds held, Aluminium of Attica will call 10 bonds at the end of the second year, 10 at the end of the third year, 10 at the end of the fourth year and 10 bonds at the end of the fifth year, it added.

The call price is 2,707 drachmas per bond at the end of the second year, 2,893 drachmas at the end of the third year, 3,103 drachmas at the end of the fourth year and 3,342 drachmas at maturity, it added.

The president of the company, Apostolos Allamanis, said that 78 percent of the proceeds will go towards retiring loans taken to finance the company's participation in the share capital increase of technical firm ALTE and the rest for working capital and machinery.
Societe Generale Bank will serve as advisor and lead underwriter for the convertible issue. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
